unchanged_frozen_unit.section: PV Sizing of a Stand Alone Solar Carport System Linked to Charging Stations and its Economic Analysis (A Case Study)
unchanged_frozen_unit.raw_text: Abstract—Electricity production from renewable energy sources mainly from solar energy, encouraged the shifting toward clean energy generation while responding to the increased energy demands of the population. This paper aims to design an off-grid photovoltaic (PV) solar carport to supply energy to electric cars. Sizing the off-grid solar carport system is to determine the number and type of solar panels, system voltage, batteries, charge regulator, and inverter size. In addition to sizing fuses and switches, combiner boxes, and the wires connecting the components of the system. In this case, the available parking area for which a solar carport is designed is $\mathbf{165~m^{2}}$ . Thus, 102 solar panels are installed which have an annual energy production of 42150KWh determined by the software System Advisor Model (SAM), where the performance of each solar panel annually decreases by $0.5\%$ . For a daily energy demand of 65KWh, 40 batteries where each battery has a capacity of 220Ah, 4 inverters where each has a power rating of 25KW, and 17 charge controllers are installed. Linking the system components is done through copper wires that their length and cross-section area are sized. The economic analysis of the system concluded that the capital investment cost of the system is 661045.36MAD, the life cycle cost (LCC) is 1460022.64MAD, the levelized cost of energy (LCOE) is 1.60MAD/KWh, and the payback period is 10.5 years. The estimated amount of the mitigated $\mathbf{CO}_{2}$ emissions for the PV system is 657347Kg/year. The results of the developed system can further be used in other applications for solar PV systems sizing.

unchanged_frozen_unit.raw_text: The shift toward clean energy generation encouraged the emergence of electric cars for their potentials in decreasing greenhouse gas emissions and shifting population behavior to less dependent on fossil fuels. Electric cars are a clean energy model of transportation prompted the development of innovative projects that provide shading and generate electricity, which are the solar photovoltaic carports linked to charging stations. Many parking lots are taking over large areas that could be covered with solar panels for energy production, and shading. The solar carports are ground-mounted structures with a slightly tilted roof area that offers a suitable platform for the solar array to be fixed [5]. These carports are stretched over cars providing adequate shading and generating energy that can be used by the electric cars for charging. Solar carports come in three types, the monopitch, duo pitch, and barrel-arch. Based on the study performed in [6], the mono-pitch type is the structure on which the PV system attain optimal energy production ana natural rain drainage.

unchanged_frozen_unit.section: A. Solar Carpot Conception and Orientation
unchanged_frozen_unit.raw_text: The designed solar carport is cost-effective as it doesn’t require a roof or a concrete surface that the PV solar array must attach to, but it only requires a steel structure. The steel structure makes the solar carport unique and reduces the cost of roof construction. According to the analysis results on the carport type and angle reported in [6]. In this case study, a mono-pitch solar carport at a tilted roof of $10^{\circ}$ is designed. The roof angle of $10^{\circ}$ is not only beneficial for optimizing the angle of the solar panels for energy generation, but also it offers natural drainage for rainwater. Furthermore, the solar panels are oriented toward the south because the case study site is in the northern hemisphere.

Furthermore, the solar panels are oriented toward the south because the case study site is in the northern hemisphere.

original_block_with_source_spans.text: Connecting the modules in parallel or in series has an impact on the array performance. If the modules are connected in parallel, the voltage of the system will be equal to the voltage of only one PV module, while the system current will add up. However, a connection in series will add up the system voltage, while the system current will be equal to the current of one PV model.

unchanged_frozen_unit.raw_text: Based on the site characteristics and the daily load energy demand of 65KWh from the electric cars. The installed standalone photovoltaic solar carport has a solar array of 102 modules with a daily power of 64.44KWh. Its annual energy production is 42150KWh as reported by SAM for the first year, which degrade by $0.5\%$ each year until the end of the useful lifetime of the PV array. The system voltage of the array is $48\mathrm{V}$ . For this system, 40 AGM batteries, each has a capacity of 220Ah are installed. 4 inverters, each having a power rating of 25KW with an efficiency of $98.30\%$ are used. The charge controller is an MPPT type of which 17 units are installed. The components of the system are linked with copper wires of different cross-section area of $120\mathrm{mm}^{2}$ that connect between the PV array the batteries and the charge controller, of $300\mathrm{mm}^{2}$ that connect the battery and the inverter, and of $25~\mathrm{mm}^{2}$ that connect the battery and the AC load. Fuses and switches in addition to combiner boxes are also sized. The economic analysis of the system indicates that a capital cost of 661045.36MAD is required. The LCC of the stand-alone solar carport is 1460022.64MAD. While the LCOE is 1.60MAD/KWh, and the payback period is 10.5 years. The amount of $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ mitigated during the system lifetime is $657347\mathrm{Kg}$ .

unchanged_frozen_unit.section: PV Sizing of a Stand Alone Solar Carport System Linked to Charging Stations and its Economic Analysis (A Case Study)
unchanged_frozen_unit.raw_text: Abstract—Electricity production from renewable energy sources mainly from solar energy, encouraged the shifting toward clean energy generation while responding to the increased energy demands of the population. This paper aims to design an off-grid photovoltaic (PV) solar carport to supply energy to electric cars. Sizing the off-grid solar carport system is to determine the number and type of solar panels, system voltage, batteries, charge regulator, and inverter size. In addition to sizing fuses and switches, combiner boxes, and the wires connecting the components of the system. In this case, the available parking area for which a solar carport is designed is $\mathbf{165~m^{2}}$ . Thus, 102 solar panels are installed which have an annual energy production of 42150KWh determined by the software System Advisor Model (SAM), where the performance of each solar panel annually decreases by $0.5\%$ . For a daily energy demand of 65KWh, 40 batteries where each battery has a capacity of 220Ah, 4 inverters where each has a power rating of 25KW, and 17 charge controllers are installed. Linking the system components is done through copper wires that their length and cross-section area are sized. The economic analysis of the system concluded that the capital investment cost of the system is 661045.36MAD, the life cycle cost (LCC) is 1460022.64MAD, the levelized cost of energy (LCOE) is 1.60MAD/KWh, and the payback period is 10.5 years. The estimated amount of the mitigated $\mathbf{CO}_{2}$ emissions for the PV system is 657347Kg/year. The results of the developed system can further be used in other applications for solar PV systems sizing.

In this case, the available parking area for which a solar carport is designed is $\mathbf{165~m^{2}}$ . Thus, 102 solar panels are installed which have an annual energy production of 42150KWh determined by the software System Advisor Model (SAM), where the performance of each solar panel annually decreases by $0.5\%$ . For a daily energy demand of 65KWh, 40 batteries where each battery has a capacity of 220Ah, 4 inverters where each has a power rating of 25KW, and 17 charge controllers are installed. Linking the system components is done through copper wires that their length and cross-section area are sized. The economic analysis of the system concluded that the capital investment cost of the system is 661045.36MAD, the life cycle cost (LCC) is 1460022.64MAD, the levelized cost of energy (LCOE) is 1.60MAD/KWh, and the payback period is 10.5 years. The estimated amount of the mitigated $\mathbf{CO}_{2}$ emissions for the PV system is 657347Kg/year. The results of the developed system can further be used in other applications for solar PV systems sizing.

unchanged_frozen_unit.raw_text: The shift toward clean energy generation encouraged the emergence of electric cars for their potentials in decreasing greenhouse gas emissions and shifting population behavior to less dependent on fossil fuels. Electric cars are a clean energy model of transportation prompted the development of innovative projects that provide shading and generate electricity, which are the solar photovoltaic carports linked to charging stations. Many parking lots are taking over large areas that could be covered with solar panels for energy production, and shading. The solar carports are ground-mounted structures with a slightly tilted roof area that offers a suitable platform for the solar array to be fixed [5]. These carports are stretched over cars providing adequate shading and generating energy that can be used by the electric cars for charging. Solar carports come in three types, the monopitch, duo pitch, and barrel-arch. Based on the study performed in [6], the mono-pitch type is the structure on which the PV system attain optimal energy production ana natural rain drainage.

In this case study, a mono-pitch solar carport at a tilted roof of $10^{\circ}$ is designed. The roof angle of $10^{\circ}$ is not only beneficial for optimizing the angle of the solar panels for energy generation, but also it offers natural drainage for rainwater. Furthermore, the solar panels are oriented toward the south because the case study site is in the northern hemisphere.

unchanged_frozen_unit.raw_text: Based on the site characteristics and the daily load energy demand of 65KWh from the electric cars. The installed standalone photovoltaic solar carport has a solar array of 102 modules with a daily power of 64.44KWh. Its annual energy production is 42150KWh as reported by SAM for the first year, which degrade by $0.5\%$ each year until the end of the useful lifetime of the PV array. The system voltage of the array is $48\mathrm{V}$ . For this system, 40 AGM batteries, each has a capacity of 220Ah are installed. 4 inverters, each having a power rating of 25KW with an efficiency of $98.30\%$ are used. The charge controller is an MPPT type of which 17 units are installed. The components of the system are linked with copper wires of different cross-section area of $120\mathrm{mm}^{2}$ that connect between the PV array the batteries and the charge controller, of $300\mathrm{mm}^{2}$ that connect the battery and the inverter, and of $25~\mathrm{mm}^{2}$ that connect the battery and the AC load. Fuses and switches in addition to combiner boxes are also sized. The economic analysis of the system indicates that a capital cost of 661045.36MAD is required. The LCC of the stand-alone solar carport is 1460022.64MAD. While the LCOE is 1.60MAD/KWh, and the payback period is 10.5 years. The amount of $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ mitigated during the system lifetime is $657347\mathrm{Kg}$ .

original_block_with_source_spans.section: H. Wiring in Series or in Parallel
original_block_with_source_spans.text: Connecting the modules in parallel or in series has an impact on the array performance. If the modules are connected in parallel, the voltage of the system will be equal to the voltage of only one PV module, while the system current will add up. However, a connection in series will add up the system voltage, while the system current will be equal to the current of one PV model.
